children: Reformation’s third-quarter net revenue rose 19.1% year over year, while the company swung to a loss from a profit. Growth in direct-to-consumer sales reflected a larger active-customer base, with wholesale demand also contributing; earnings were weighed by higher operating expenses, IPO-related stock compensation, a debt-extinguishment loss and discrete tax charges.
¹ Reported as “Net revenue”. ² Reported as “Net income (loss)”. ³ Reported as “Diluted”.
: DTC net revenue increased 16.7% and Wholesale and Other net revenue rose 40.8%, driven by increased demand from existing wholesale partners.
: Active Customers reached approximately 1.3 million, up 23% from the third quarter of 2025; DTC Net Revenue per Customer declined 0.5% to $419.
: Increased to 60.4% from 57.9%, primarily reflecting lower average tariff rates, vendor concessions and higher average unit retail.
: Store count grew to 77 from 60, with 13 new openings and no closures during the 39 weeks ended September 26, 2026.
